name: Free Lunch Lab: AI company profits, last four quarters
description: Quarterly net and operating income of nine AI-related companies from their filings, with market values, paper gains on AI stakes and the source of each figure.
license: CC BY 4.0 (figures from the company filings and other sources named in each entry)
about: AI companies' profits shared out per person, for the essay ai-company-profits-per-person. Money in US$ millions unless a key says otherwise (UsdBn = billions, KrwBn = billions of won, TwdM = millions of NT$). Net income is GAAP/IFRS net income as reported (attributable to the parent where relevant); operating income is GAAP operating income (TSMC: income from operations). src/ai-profits.js sums the four quarters of each company (the last four reported), divides by the world population in data/billionaires-2026.json, compares with the site's $3.00-a-day line from the calculator data (src/calc-world.js) and fills the {{aip.…}} numbers in the essay, the X images and the checks in build.js. Quarters marked derived = full year minus the other three quarters.

yenMarket.note: approximate market rate on 13 Nov 2026 from the research notes (no primary source recorded); the essay uses the site's 2025 World Bank rate for its yen figures and quotes this only to show how much the rate has moved

proposals.name: Sam Altman, "Moore's Law for Everything" (March 2021): American Equity Fund
proposals.rate: 2.5% of market value a year for companies above a certain valuation, paid in shares; plus 2.5% of the value of privately held land, paid in dollars
proposals.payoutClaim: "a decade from now each of the 250 million adults in America would get about $13,500 every year"

proposals.name: Anthropic Public Benefit Fund (18 Oct 2026)
proposals.rate: 5% of Anthropic shares committed (subject to stockholder approval); board may add 2% for every 50% increase in value above a baseline; uses may include "direct distributions to specific populations"

proposals.name: US H.R. 10044 (Sara Jacobs, Greg Casar, Valerie Foushee; September 2026)
proposals.rate: excise tax on major AI companies, the higher of 2% of the value of AI tokens or 3% of AI-services revenue while unemployment is 5% or less, rising with unemployment (schedule not given in the article); proceeds to job creation, not cash
proposals.caveat: rates from Fortune's description; bill text not read

proposals.name: OECD/G20 Pillar Two global minimum tax
proposals.rate: 15% minimum effective tax rate for groups with revenue over EUR 750m, applied from 2024
proposals.caveat: a floor on corporate tax, not an AI tax; the 15% scenario here applies it to after-tax profit, which these firms have already been taxed on

proposals.name: OpenAI, "Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age" (April 2026)
proposals.rate: no rate: floats a public wealth fund, higher taxes on capital/AI returns and a robot tax

proposals.name: Karsten Wildberger, German digital minister (Tagesspiegel interview, Oct 2026, via dts)
proposals.rate: no rate: "Den extrem hohen Umsatz mit dieser Technologie müssen wir besteuern"

proposals.name: Anthropic economic policy framework (2026)
proposals.rate: no rate: mentions "new sources of tax revenue", sovereign wealth models and equity-sharing in a high-unemployment scenario

caveats: Fiscal years differ; FY totals mix years ending Nov 2025 to Sep 2026. Prefer TTM.

Net income includes non-AI business (Apple almost entirely; Amazon retail; Microsoft Office; Meta ads; Alphabet search) and large paper gains on stakes in AI labs (Alphabet, Amazon, NVIDIA, Microsoft).
Profits are after corporate tax; the 15% and 25% scenarios are shares of after-tax profit, not tax rates on pre-tax profit.
Much of this profit is already spent on capex (Amazon alone $215bn over its last four quarters) and buybacks; taking 100% would leave nothing for either, and share prices would not stay put.
Market caps: Yahoo Finance closes x SEC cover-page share counts (dates differ by up to ~2.5 months; TSMC uses its 31 Dec 2025 count). Alphabet Class B and Meta Class B valued at Class A prices.
Yen figures use the 2025 World Bank rate (149.66), the rate the site uses; the spot rate on 13 Nov 2026 was about 159.9.
TSMC quarterly conversion uses each quarter's NT$/US$ revenue ratio (31.0-32.0); FY2025 uses the 20-F convenience rate 31.37.

Operating income is before interest, investment gains and tax. For Alphabet and Amazon it is far below net income because of paper gains on stakes in AI labs (largely Anthropic and SpaceX); for Meta and Broadcom it is above net income. Meta's $9.89bn settlement charge sits inside operating income.
"Paper gains" total includes Microsoft's whole other income line (not only investment gains) and Amazon's whole other income line; treat the share as approximate.
